# Command reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_command_docs.py — do not edit by hand. -->

Commands start with `%` at the beginning of the input (a line starting with `%` is essentially never valid shell).
Inside shtick, `%help name` shows the same details.

## General

### `%clear`, `%cls`

Clear the screen.

### `%config`

Show or change settings: %config · %config name · %config name=value.

```text
Settings for this session. To keep them, put them in config.toml (see %config).
```

### `%editmode`, `%vi`, `%emacs`

Switch key bindings: %editmode vi|emacs (or %vi / %emacs).

### `%exit`, `%quit`

Leave shtick.

### `%help`

Keys and commands · %help name for one command.

### `%restart`

Restart the shell session (clears variables, functions, options).

### `%shell`

Show or switch the session's shell: %shell dash · %shell /bin/bash.

```text
Switching starts a fresh session in the same directory: variables, functions and options don't carry over.
```

### `%theme`

List or switch color themes: %theme · %theme nebula.

### `%tty`

Run cells attached to a terminal (merges stdout and stderr): %tty on|off.

```text
For programs that check [ -t 1 ] or only print colors on a terminal. stderr is merged into stdout.
```

## Scripts & tracing

### `%close`

Close the open script.

### `%edit`

Edit the open script (or FILE) in $EDITOR and reload it: %edit [FILE].

### `%goto`

Move the open script's position: %goto N (command number) · %goto +N / -N.

### `%next`, `%n`

Run the next command of the open script: %next [N].

### `%open`

Open a script to step through it: %open FILE [args…].

```text
Splits FILE into top-level commands (functions, if/for blocks and heredocs stay whole).
args become the positional parameters ($1, $2, …) in the session.
Then: %next runs the next command · %step puts it in the input to edit first · %run runs the rest.
```

### `%run`

Run the rest of the open script, or open and run a file: %run [-k] [--all] [FILE [args…]].

```text
-k      keep going after a failing command
--all   start from the first command
```

### `%script`, `%where`

Show the open script's commands and the current position.

### `%step`, `%s`

Put the next command of the open script into the input, to edit before running.

### `%trace`

Run code with set -x and show each executed command: %trace [code] · body on next lines.

```text
%trace                 trace the previous cell again
%trace CODE            trace CODE
%trace --next          trace the open script's next command
%trace FILE [args…]    trace a whole script file

Each command is listed with its line, nesting and function, with variables expanded,
separately from the output.
```

## Linting, sandbox & tests

### `%expect`

Check the last cell and record it for %test: %expect exit 0 · stdout contains "done".

```text
exit N · exit != N · exit nonzero · ok · fails
stdout|stderr|output  contains TEXT · not-contains TEXT · equals TEXT · matches REGEX · empty · not-empty · lines N
file exists PATH · file missing PATH · file contains PATH TEXT · dir exists PATH
duration < 2s · duration < 500ms
sandbox changed PATH · sandbox unchanged

%expect           list the last cell's expectations
%expect --clear   remove them
```

### `%lint`

Shellcheck report for the last cell, a file, or the open script: %lint [FILE | script | N].

```text
%lint           the previous cell
%lint N         cell N
%lint FILE      a file
%lint script    the open script

While typing, the most important finding is shown in the key bar (%config lint=off to hide it).
Codes in the lint_exclude setting are skipped (cells often use variables set in other cells).
```

### `%sandbox`

Run cells in a throwaway directory and show what they change: %sandbox on [--copy] · off · status.

```text
%sandbox on          an empty temporary directory
%sandbox on --copy   a temporary copy of the current directory
%sandbox off         go back to the original directory and delete the sandbox

After each cell, files created (+), modified (~) and deleted (−) are listed.
It's a working-directory sandbox, not a security boundary: absolute paths and cd reach outside.
```

### `%save-test`

Save the recorded cells and expectations as a test file: %save-test FILE [-f].

```text
Run it later with: shtick test FILE (exits non-zero on failure — for CI).
The file is a shell script: cells are separated by #%% lines, expectations are #% expect comments.
```

### `%test`

Re-run the recorded cells in a fresh session and check their expectations: %test · %test reset.

```text
Runs every cell since the session started (or since %test reset) in a new session of the same
shell, in a fresh sandbox if the sandbox is on (otherwise in the directory shtick started in),
and checks each cell's %expect lines. Cells without expectations still run, as setup.

%test reset      start recording from here
%test list       show what would run
```

## History & saving

### `%history`, `%hist`

Show history: %history [-n] [-g pattern] [-l N] [range].

```text
ranges: 4 · 4-6 · 4:7 (exclusive) · ~1/ (previous session) · ~1/2-3 · several separated by spaces

-n          show cell numbers
-g PATTERN  search all sessions (glob; plain text matches anywhere)
-l N        the last N entries
-s          show exit statuses
```

### `%recall`

Put an earlier cell (or a range) into the input for editing: %recall [range].

### `%rerun`

Run earlier cells again: %rerun [range] · -l N the last N.

### `%save`

Write successful cells into a script: %save FILE [range] [-a] [-f].

```text
ranges: 4 · 4-6 · 4:7 (exclusive) · ~1/ (previous session) · ~1/2-3 · several separated by spaces

Without a range: every cell of this session that exited 0. %commands are never included.
-a   include cells that failed
-f   overwrite FILE

The script starts with a shebang for the session's shell (setting: save_shebang) and is made executable.
```

## Variables & portability

### `%compare`

Run code in fresh sessions of several shells, side by side: %compare [shells…] [-- code].

```text
%compare bash dash zsh -- echo $((1 + 1))
%compare /bin/bash bash        the previous cell, in macOS's bash 3.2 and Homebrew's bash
%compare                       the previous cell in every installed shell
%compare dash zsh              …with the code on the following lines

Each shell gets a new session in its own empty temporary directory (--here: the current directory).
Rows that differ between shells are highlighted.
```

### `%vars`

Variables and functions this session defined or changed: %vars · %vars NAME · -a all.

```text
Compares the shell's variables and functions with how they were when the session started:
+ defined · ~ changed · − unset. Shell-managed variables (RANDOM, LINENO, PWD…) are left out.
%vars NAME   show one declaration in full
-a          list every variable, not just the changes
```
